evals.prompt: Everyone on the team agrees the codebase is a mess and nobody agrees what to do about it. I have budget for roughly one engineer-month. Tell me what we should spend it on, and then start making the change.
evals.expected_output: Two jobs the roster does not split, and the request explicitly asks for both. Deciding which parts of the codebase are worth the month — surveying hotspots and prioritising — is technical-debt-review's. Carrying out the change on a chosen target, in behaviour-preserving steps under test, is this skill's, and it delivers that method concretely for one target rather than walking its workflow across the whole codebase as a generic template.
assertions: Separates the two halves: deciding which parts of the codebase are worth the month, versus carrying out the change on one of them
Refers to technical-debt-review for surveying the codebase and prioritising where the month goes
Delivers the refactoring half itself — how a chosen target is changed safely, in steps — rather than deferring the whole request
Does not walk its own workflow across the entire codebase as a generic template
States the boundary: debt review decides what to work on, while refactoring is how the chosen code changes without altering behaviour
